clue.text: Recording capital exchanges, party fudges ledgers

indicators.note: the instruction is to note down an exchange of capitals, the opening letters of the next two words' synonyms swapping places

parts.note: a bash is an informal word for a party
to cook the books is to fudge them, so cooks means fudges

explanation.surface: A political party is fiddling its accounts, the ledgers that record capital changing hands.
explanation.walkthrough: A Spoonerism without Spooner: 'Recording capital exchanges' tells you to swap the initial letters of BASH COOKS. 'Recording capital exchanges' also looks like the definition, but the ledgers come last.
explanation.definitionFit: These are account books in which a business enters every receipt and payment of money, a kind of ledger.

clue.text: Restrict stuff on page

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second, so one goes on the other

parts.note: to cram is to stuff something full

explanation.surface: An instruction to restrict how much material is crammed onto a single page.
explanation.definitionFit: To hamper or confine is the verb sense, as in cramping someone's style.

clue.text: Having a Scotch, perhaps, en route's a weakness

parts.note: a short is a small measure of spirits such as whisky, Scotch being one example
on the way, arriving, coming

explanation.surface: Someone admits that drinking whisky on the journey is their weak spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' marks Scotch as one example of a short, a British name for a measure of spirits as opposed to beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A failing or defect in someone's character is a synonym for a weakness.

clue.text: British formed pairs, heading off in a group

indicators.note: the head, or first letter, of the word for formed pairs is taken off

parts.note: things matched are put together in pairs

explanation.surface: British troops pair up and set off together as a group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' looks like departing; it removes the first letter, M, from MATCHED.
explanation.definitionFit: Items gathered and processed together form a batch, so they are handled collectively.

clue.text: Established novelist makes short broadcast

indicators.note: something broadcast is heard rather than read, so the words are taken by their sound

parts.note: a novelist is an author, and to make short is to dock, as with a tail; author docks spoken in a non-rhotic accent gives the entry

explanation.surface: A well-known novelist produces a brief radio piece.
explanation.walkthrough: The sound match only works without a pronounced R, as in standard southern British speech: AUTHOR DOCKS.
explanation.definitionFit: Conventional, accepted and traditional views are established ones, the sense of conforming to custom.

clue.text: He stops believer becoming leader of another faith

indicators.note: the pronoun plugs, or stops, the gap in the believer, sitting inside it

parts.note: a Sikh is a believer in Sikhism
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man prevents a religious follower from converting and heading a rival religion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another faith' is fair because the wordplay already uses a Sikh; the answer heads an Islamic community.
explanation.definitionFit: An Arab chief or Muslim religious head, so a leader in a faith other than Sikhism.

clue.text: Sacred song, second to be introduced to mate before mass

indicators.note: the letter is brought into the middle of the friend word

parts.note: a pal is a mate, a friend
M is the physics symbol for mass

explanation.surface: A hymn, with a friend coming in second, sung ahead of the church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mass' looks ecclesiastical but is just M, the physics symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: The Book of Psalms is a collection of sacred songs or hymns from the Bible.

clue.text: Pawn? Come back to take it

parts.note: P is the chess notation for a pawn
to resume is to come back to something after a break

explanation.surface: A chess player challenges an opponent to take back a pawn.
explanation.definitionFit: To assume or suppose something, as in I take it you agree, is the same idea.

clue.text: Arsenic, poisoner's top killer

parts.note: As is the chemical symbol for arsenic

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter

explanation.surface: Arsenic is the first-choice deadly weapon for a poisoner.
explanation.definitionFit: A venomous snake, such as the one that killed Cleopatra, is a deadly creature.

clue.text: Flash queen confined to vile single-sex establishment

parts.note: a flash is a moment, informally a mo

indicators.note: the royal letters are shut up within the word for vile

parts.note: something nasty is vile
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: A brief view of the monarch locked up in some horrid men-only or women-only institution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flash' suggests showing off; it is only MO, a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: A community of monks lives there, typically all men, making it a single-sex establishment.

clue.text: A female splitting collection up

indicators.note: the letter for female breaks the word for collection into two

parts.note: a lot is a set of items, as at an auction

explanation.surface: A woman breaks up a gathering of items.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' sits at the end looking like part of 'splitting up'; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: High overhead or in the air is the meaning, the same as up.

clue.text: Re-open hut, possibly, with that

indicators.note: possibly suggests a different arrangement of the letters of the words before it

explanation.surface: An instruction to reopen a shed, perhaps along with another one.
explanation.definitionFit: Immediately after that, at which point, is the meaning, as is the phrase with that.

clue.text: Task ends, hemming length on stretch covers

parts.note: a patch is a stretch of time or ground, as in a bad patch
work is a task to be done

indicators.note: hemming in means surrounding, so the word for ends encloses the letter

parts.note: quits means stops or ends

explanation.surface: Sewing language: finishing off a task, hemming a length of fabric, while working on stretch covers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hemming' and 'stretch covers' make a sewing scene; 'on' just places the stretch first.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedspreads made of sewn-together scraps of fabric are covers for a bed.

clue.text: Cash that must be taken on reform, tip included

parts.note: in cricket the on side is also called the leg side

indicators.note: the word for tip is held within the word for reform

parts.note: to alter is to change or reform
a tip is an end, as of a finger

explanation.surface: A demand that money be accepted for reform, with a gratuity added.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is cricket: the leg side of the field, where the batter stands, is also called the on side.
explanation.definitionFit: Money that a creditor is legally obliged to accept in payment of a debt.

clue.text: Busybody going round with doctor's plant

indicators.note: the busybody goes round, enclosing, the other letters

parts.note: a snoop is a nosy person, a busybody

explanation.surface: A nosy neighbour drops in at the GP's surgery with a pot plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' gives W, a standard abbreviation, rather than linking the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A small white-flowered bulb flowering in late winter is a plant.

clue.text: Show enables MC to appear in new guise

indicators.note: a new guise is a different form, so these letters take a fresh order

explanation.surface: A television show lets its host come on in disguise.
explanation.definitionFit: An outward appearance or show, often a false one, as in a semblance of order.

clue.text: Spare silver slipped between adjacent notes

indicators.note: the metal is slid in among the two notes

parts.note: me is the third note of the sol-fa scale
re is the second note of the sol-fa scale, next to me
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Some spare silver coins fall between two neighbouring banknotes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notes' look like banknotes; they are sol-fa notes. 'Spare' is the adjective meaning scanty.
explanation.definitionFit: Spare as an adjective means lean or scanty, the sense of inadequate in amount.

clue.text: Proscribed part of speech frequently lacking force

parts.note: a verb is one of the parts of speech

indicators.note: the word for frequently goes without the force symbol

parts.note: often means frequently
F is the physics symbol for force

explanation.surface: A grammarian bans a part of speech that often lacks power.
explanation.definitionFit: German for forbidden, used in English for something banned or prohibited.

clue.text: Poster displaying US author

definitions.meaning: one who posts letters or parcels
Norman ..., the American novelist of The Naked and the Dead

explanation.surface: A billboard advertising an American writer.
explanation.definitionFit: One who sends post is a sender by mail; Norman Mailer was a famous American novelist.

clue.text: European royal house detailed unknown form of English

indicators.note: de-tailed, with the tail or last letter cut off

parts.note: the Stuarts were a royal house of Scotland and England
y is an unknown in algebra

explanation.surface: A European royal house detailed an unknown form of English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' looks like 'described in detail' but means de-tailed, losing the final T.
explanation.definitionFit: Estuary English is the accent of London and the Thames estuary area, a variety of English.

clue.text: Hardly any, it's said, idle under Medieval system

indicators.note: it's said marks words taken by how they are spoken

parts.note: few means hardly any; spoken, it gives the first syllable
to dally is to idle or dawdle

explanation.surface: In the Middle Ages almost nobody was allowed to laze about.
explanation.definitionFit: Feudalism was the medieval system of lords and vassals, so this adverb means in that manner.

clue.text: Party men, dull, not the type to fight back

definitions.text: not the type to fight back

parts.note: a do is a party
OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers, men
mat or matt means dull, not glossy

explanation.surface: Party men, dull, who never retaliate.
explanation.walkthrough: OR, other ranks, is the military term for soldiers who are not officers.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who lets others walk all over them never resists, a figurative sense.

clue.text: Alien following ship in publicly funded trip

indicators.note: the alien comes after the ship

parts.note: a junk is a Chinese sailing ship
ET is the extraterrestrial of the film

explanation.surface: An extraterrestrial trailing a vessel on a taxpayer-funded jaunt.
explanation.definitionFit: A jaunt by officials at public expense, a free trip, is the sense here.

clue.text: Bumbling moth let out when we got it

indicators.note: out signals that the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: A clumsy moth is released from a lamp just as we realise something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bumbling' looks like an anagram signal, but it is fodder; 'out' is the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden moment of understanding or inspiration, when we finally grasp the point.

clue.text: Shrinking fabric finally cut up

indicators.note: in a down clue up means reading from bottom to top
the final letter of the fabric word is cut off

parts.note: dimity is a striped cotton fabric

explanation.surface: Cloth that shrinks when it is at last cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally cut' turns DIMITY into DIMIT; 'up' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Shy and shrinking describe someone easily frightened, an adjective sense.

clue.text: Demand for product on ground-breaking course

indicators.note: the demand comes on, after, the word for ground-breaking

parts.note: something ground-breaking is new
a market is demand for goods, as in there is no market for it

explanation.surface: Demand for an innovative product on a pioneering course of study.
explanation.walkthrough: NEWMARKET is a famous British racecourse in Suffolk, home of horse racing.
explanation.definitionFit: A racecourse is a course, and Newmarket is perhaps the best known in Britain.

clue.text: Trouble's over between playing partners

indicators.note: the cricket letter is placed between the two partners

parts.note: West and East are partners in a game of bridge
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: Trouble is over between two players who were partners.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, West and East play as partners against North and South.
explanation.definitionFit: Distress, grief and misfortune are woe; trouble is a near synonym.

clue.text: Lines bridging tiny distance forming connector

indicators.note: the lines span the gap between the two letters of the distance, sitting inside

parts.note: mm is a millimetre, a tiny distance
an ode is a poem, lines of verse

explanation.surface: Lines spanning a minute gap make a link.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lines' looks like cables; it is a poem.
explanation.definitionFit: A device linking a computer to a phone line is a connector to the network.

clue.text: Each end of race precise

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

parts.note: very means precise, as in at that very moment

explanation.surface: Every race finish is timed to the exact moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Every and each both mean all members of a group individually.

clue.text: Stained metal dart ultimately pierces better

parts.note: tin is a metal

indicators.note: the letter goes into the word for better, piercing it as a dart would

parts.note: cured means made better, healed

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A metal dart that has pierced something has become stained.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinged or coloured with a dye or tint, a stained surface is the sense.
